## Warm-up 🔥 (5 min)

Have you ever had files like this?

```
thesis.docx
thesis_final.docx
thesis_final_v2.docx
thesis_final_v2_REALLY_FINAL.docx
thesis_final_v2_REALLY_FINAL_fixed_by_supervisor.docx
```

. . .

Write in the chat: **which one is the real one?** 🤔

::: notes
0–10 min. Quick laugh + chat discussion. Lead to the question: how do we keep history without chaos?
:::

# What is version control?

## Git = a lab notebook for your files 📓

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Lab notebook**

- Date of every experiment
- What you changed and why
- You never tear out pages
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Git**

- **Commit** = a dated snapshot
- **Message** = what & why
- History is never lost
:::
::::

## Three words for today

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Repository** (repo) | A project folder with its whole history |
| **Commit** | A saved snapshot + a message |
| **GitHub** | A website that stores your repo online |

. . .

Git ≠ GitHub. **Git** is the tool, **GitHub** is where we keep the copy.

::: notes
10–25 min block of "something new". Keep it under 15 min total.
:::

## Exercise 1: First repository 🐙 {.smaller}

⏱️ 15 min

1. On GitHub click **New repository** → name it `programming-basics`
2. ✅ *Add a README file* → **Create repository**
3. Click ✏️ on `README.md` and add:
```markdown
   # Programming Basics
   My name is ... and I study ...
```
4. Write a message → **Commit changes**
5. Click **History** 🕒 — what do you see?

✅ React when you see your commit · 💡 **Bonus:** make a second change and compare

::: notes
25–40 min. Everyone works on their own screen, you watch the reactions; ask anyone with ✋ to share their screen.
:::

# The terminal — the bare minimum

## Opening the terminal 💻

- **Windows:** *Git Bash*
- **macOS:** *Terminal*
- **Linux:** *Terminal*

```bash
pwd        # where am I?
ls         # what is here?
cd Desktop # go into a folder
cd ..      # go one level up
mkdir kse  # make a new folder
```

::: notes
Live coding: students tell you in the chat what to type. Zoom in the terminal font (Ctrl/Cmd +). Show that typos give errors and that's fine.
:::

## Exercise 2: Find your way (5 min)

1. Check where you are: `pwd`
2. List files: `ls`
3. Go to your Desktop (or Documents)
4. Create a folder `kse` and go inside it
5. Check with `pwd` that you are there ✅

# From your laptop to GitHub

## One-time setup ⚙️

Tell Git who you are:

```bash
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
```

. . .

Use the **same e-mail** as on GitHub.

::: notes
Authentication for push: decide beforehand! Options:
- GitHub CLI: `gh auth login` (easiest if installed)
- Git Credential Manager (comes with Git for Windows — browser login pops up)
- Personal Access Token
This step can easily eat 15+ minutes — have a helper or a plan B (web upload).
:::

## The Git cycle 🔄

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5em; flex-wrap:wrap; margin-top:1.5em; font-family:monospace; font-size:0.9em;">
  <div style="border:2px solid #888; border-radius:10px; padding:0.4em 0.7em;">git clone</div>
  <span>→</span>
  <div style="border:2px solid #42affa; border-radius:10px; padding:0.4em 0.7em;">✏️ edit files</div>
  <span>→</span>
  <div style="border:2px solid #42affa; border-radius:10px; padding:0.4em 0.7em;">git add</div>
  <span>→</span>
  <div style="border:2px solid #42affa; border-radius:10px; padding:0.4em 0.7em;">git commit</div>
  <span>→</span>
  <div style="border:2px solid #42affa; border-radius:10px; padding:0.4em 0.7em;">git push</div>
</div>
<p style="text-align:center; margin-top:1em; font-size:0.8em;">
  ↩️ <span style="color:#42affa;">then back to <b>edit files</b> — again and again</span>
</p>
<p style="text-align:center; margin-top:1.5em; font-size:0.6em; color:#aaa;">
  <code>git clone</code> only once · the blue part every time you work
</p>
```

## The commands

```bash
# 1. Copy your repo to your laptop (once)
git clone https://github.com/<username>/programming-basics.git
cd programming-basics

# 2. After changing files
git status                     # what changed?
git add about_me.md            # choose what to save
git commit -m "Add about me"   # take the snapshot
git push                       # send it to GitHub
```

## Exercise 3: About me 🎉 {.smaller}

⏱️ 20 min · Breakout rooms · one **shares the screen** and types, one guides — **then switch**

1. In the folder `kse`: `git clone` your repo, then `cd programming-basics`
2. Create `about_me.md` with: your name, favourite organism 🦠, one thing you want to learn
3. `git status` → `git add` → `git commit` → `git push`
4. Refresh GitHub — is your file there? Post your repo link in the chat 🔗

💡 **Bonus:** change the file again, make a second commit and look at `git log`

::: notes
40–70 min (incl. setup + cycle slides). Paste the steps in the chat before opening rooms. Visit rooms one by one.
Biggest risks: authentication on push, cloning into the wrong folder.
Plan B for anyone stuck: upload the file via the GitHub website so they still leave with a commit.
Plan C if many laptops fail: GitHub Codespaces (terminal in the browser, Git already logged in).
:::

# Wrap-up

## What we did today ✅

- Created a **repository** on GitHub
- Used the **terminal**: `pwd`, `ls`, `cd`, `mkdir`
- Made our first **commit** and **push**

. . .

> From now on, **every class ends with a commit.**

## Cheat sheet 📌

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git clone <url>` | Copy a repo to your laptop |
| `git status` | Show what changed |
| `git add <file>` | Choose files to save |
| `git commit -m "..."` | Save a snapshot |
| `git push` | Send commits to GitHub |
| `git log` | Show history |
